page.layout: One page of running text in one column, with marginal notes in the right margin. The left strip of the scan is the edge of the facing page and is left out.

main_text.p: (Aristotelem iterum auditis). Petacem facit popu-lum, ne dicam petulantem, (res ipsa clamat, experti sumus nimirum jamdiu,) & cuncta moven-tem, si Legislatorem facilem hac ex parte, & ad vota libidinémque populi jure suo cedentem re-pererint. Reprehendit igitur jure merito & gra-viter, ibidem summus Philosophus Legem Hippo-damí cujusdam Milefii Legislatoris; [illegible, ~8 letters] illam quidem, primo aspectu speciosam satis, & plausibilem vulgo, ut qui aliquid utile civitati invenirent publico praemio afficerentur, sed si pe-nitius intueare, nec prudentem omninò, nec falu-tarem. Quid enim ferè excogitari potest ad pub-licas res turbandas opportunius, quàm quòd pro-posito praemio invitentur homines factiofi, vafri & turbulenti ingenii, [illegible, ~8 letters] νόμων λύσιν ἢ πολιτείας, ὡς κοινὸν ἀγαθόν, ut sub specie boni pub-lici, non eversionem modò legum inducere, sed & totius civilis administrationis formam, sub in-eundem revocatam, & in novam ideam pro suo ubitu? refictam, civitati obtrudere studeant? Phi-losophume obsecro videmini vobis audire suis tem-poribus illustrem; an Vatem potiùs, eorum qui nunc sunt morum hominumque praescium ac prae-nuncium; Tertiò, quum Legum immutatio tollendi præsentis alicujus incommodi gratia instituatur; & fieri possit, ut ex istâ immutatione suboriantur, imò vix fieri possit ut non suboriantur,) & emer-gant tandem, utut fortassis occulta initio, plura & graviora incommoda: [illegible, ~10 letters], Graviora inquit idem gravissimus Philosophus. Omninòinferre vul-nera dum minoribus modo desidera-mus. Ambr. 2 Offic. 2. ducens aliqua incommoda, eáque non levia, in Rep. tolerare & perferre; (quod idem & de Ecclesiâ, quæ & ipsa Respublica quædam est, saluendum est:) quàm obtentu Reformationis sive Ecclesiasticæ sive Politicæ, vetera instituta soli-tare, leges refigere, τὰ ἄνω κάτω sursum vorsum omnia

page.notes: The right margin notes are printed in small type beside the text. The Greek word after "Hippodami" and the Greek in the "ubitu" phrase are badly rubbed and only partly legible. "ubitu" is printed as a fragment: the first letters are lost in the scan, so the word is marked with [?]. The fragment at "Phi-/losophume" is printed as shown. Ink is blurred around the middle of the page, and the text is read from the clearest parts. The left edge strip belongs to the neighbouring page and is not transcribed.
